assumptions: The pictured sign-in email address is the account identifier for the proposed reset-request form; no separate recovery identifier is specified.
The wireframe establishes appearance and affordances only, not implemented navigation, authentication, validation, masking semantics, accessibility behavior, or recovery pages.
Recovery-screen layout, copy, and routes are not prescribed. The proposed screens and states are design suggestions, not observed implementation.
Synthetic accounts and an in-memory notification sink provide prototype link inspection and notification recording; neither an external delivery channel nor a visitor-facing sink view is assumed.
No additional password policy, persistent account storage, sign-in behavior, or particular session mechanism is assumed.

The approved requirements use REQ-001 through REQ-018; their prior-stage output has no returned standalone source-reference locator, so identifiers are linked without a fabricated stage_output reference.

findings.statement: The 480×360 white wireframe depicts a narrow dark-bordered sign-in panel centered horizontally, with a Sign in heading, a labeled Email address text field showing the name@example.com placeholder, a labeled Password field with a masked sample, a full-width dark Sign in button, and muted 'No account? Contact your administrator.' footer. This depicts content, not a functioning sign-in implementation.

A blue underlined 'Forgot password?' link appears below the password field. Only the visible recovery entry affordance is pictured; the wireframe does not show its destination or a working transition.

Provide a server-rendered sign-in entry where the pictured Forgot password? control navigates to a reset-request page. Treat email and password as sign-in inputs; propose associated errors for empty fields and malformed email, a nondouble-submitting progress state, and an intelligible failure state. Sign-in authentication behavior beyond the link is unresolved, not observed.

The unpictured server-rendered reset-request screen accepts an email account identifier and offers a submit action and route back to sign-in. Propose empty or malformed input errors before submission, neutral in-progress and retryable failure states, and no disclosure of whether an identifier is registered. The email identifier is inferred from the pictured sign-in field, not specified by a recovery mockup.

The unpictured request-confirmation screen gives identical visitor-facing outcomes for equivalent requests for existing and nonexistent accounts; propose a neutral confirmation and retry route that do not reveal link issuance or sink contents. Treat an over-limit request without account-disclosing copy. This screen has no required input; propose neutral fallback for an absent result, announced in-flight transition if used, and a nondisclosing error/retry state.

Behind reset-request and confirmation pages, enforce at most five link-issuing requests per synthetic account per hour; eligible requests record a reset link in the in-memory notification sink and unknown or over-limit requests do not issue another account link. This is backend/delivery behavior, not a pictured screen, visitor inbox, or observable proof of enforcement.

An eligible link obtained through the prototype sink opens an unpictured server-rendered new-password form with a labeled new-password field and submit action while the link is unused and strictly before its issue time plus 30 minutes. Propose an empty-field error, an announced submitting state that prevents duplicates, and a retryable processing error without claiming a password-strength policy or visually verified link validity.

For an invalid, already-used, or expired link (at or after issuance plus 30 minutes), prevent a second password change and show an unpictured invalid-link state with a route to request another link. Suggest a neutral fallback for absent state and announced loading only if navigation has an in-flight phase; explain inability to use the link without disclosing account data.

A successful valid reset replaces the old password once and transitions to an unpictured success screen with clear completion feedback and a proposed path to sign-in. The completion screen has no required input; propose a neutral fallback for missing result, announced transition if loading, and retry guidance for processing errors rather than false success. No post-reset sign-in behavior is established by the wireframe.

After every successful reset, invalidate all active sessions of that account and record an owner-addressed notification in the in-memory sink. These are background effects, not observed screen contents; the proposed completion screen need not expose session internals, the link, notification records, or a delivery provider.

For pictured and proposed screens, implement keyboard-operable controls, logical focus and visible focus indicators; programmatically associate labels and accessible names with inputs, links, and buttons; associate and announce errors, announce status changes, move focus to new confirmation/error headings, and verify text, control, and focus contrast including the pictured blue link and muted footer. Pictured visual labels and colors do not establish actual accessibility or contrast compliance.

Technical and delivery constraints have no visually demonstrable coverage in the wireframe: use Python 3.12, Flask request handling and server-rendered sign-in/recovery pages; provide pytest coverage for the required reset behavior; document synthetic-account and in-memory-sink production limitations; do not deploy or add a deployment workflow. These need implementation, test, or documentation verification rather than screenshot assertions.
